answer.generated: Semaphore-based solutions can prevent deadlock in a scenario where two processes share reusable resources by ensuring that access to these resources is managed in a controlled manner. Specifically, a semaphore initialized to the number of available resources can be used to allow processes to request access (using the P operation) and release resources when done (via the V operation). If both processes attempt to access the resource simultaneously but the semaphore indicates no resources are available, one or both will block until a resource becomes free, thus preventing the circular wait condition that leads to deadlock.
